chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Dawud al-Raqqi, from a man from his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whichever believer visits a believer for the sake of God, Mighty and Majestic, during his illness, God will appoint for him an angel from the visitors who will visit him in his grave and seek forgiveness for him until the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.العوّاد: The visitors (of the sick) — a class of angels designated for visiting the ill
key_terms.عاد: Visited (the sick) — 'iyada, the Islamic practice of visiting the ill, considered highly meritorious
key_terms.في الله: For the sake of God — sincerity of intention, doing good for God's pleasure alone
key_terms.يستغفر: Seeks forgiveness — the angel continuously prays for the visitor's forgiveness in their grave

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting a sick Muslim according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that visiting a sick fellow believer purely for God's sake carries a profound divine reward: God assigns a dedicated angel to that visitor who will continue visiting them in their grave and interceding for their forgiveness until the Day of Judgment. This hadith was transmitted to the early Shia community through a chain that includes Dawud al-Raqqi, a trusted companion of the Imam, emphasizing the immense spiritual weight of this act of brotherly care in Islamic social ethics.
